editorial:
Imagine walking through a quiet, sunny forest with someone you love, but instead of just chatting, you are recording every single word on an old tape machine. That is exactly what you get with this unique story. You follow Carlo, an older man, and his young girlfriend as they spend the day together on the edge of the city. The whole vibe is very relaxed and intimate, making you feel like you are spying on a private conversation. It is less about a big plot and more about the feeling of a relationship and the way these two people communicate with each other in nature.

What really sticks with you is the acting, especially from Carlo Cecchi, who makes the character feel very real and human. The pacing is slow, which might be a turn-off if you want big explosions, but it works perfectly for this kind of mood. If you enjoy artistic films that take their time, you will love this.
endingExplained: As the day comes to a close, the recording process reveals the true tension between the couple. You realize the interview was not just for fun, but a way for Carlo to dig into the truth of their relationship. The movie ends with a feeling of uncertainty, leaving you to wonder if the tape recorded a happy memory or the beginning of the end for them. It wraps up quietly, focusing on the silence after the recording stops.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves slow cinema and deep conversations.
